text:
Matthew Schaefer is a teenager, and he just did something only two other teenage defensemen in NHL history had done, per Daily Faceoff: he scored a hat trick. The Islanders' 2025 first overall pick put nine shots on goal in 23:24 and turned a tight game into a 5-1 rout of Columbus. As NHL.com's Stefen Rosner pointed out, it is the second night in a row an Islander has had three, after Simon Holmstrom did it against Anaheim, and Schaefer has six points in his last two games.

For two periods there was nothing to separate these teams. Expected goals (the quality of the chances) were 0.97 to 0.94 in the first and 1.36 to 1.29 in the second. The Islanders were simply sharper with theirs. Anthony Duclair scored on the power play with 58 seconds left in the first, and Schaefer's first, an unassisted wrister 94 seconds into the second, came on a 6% chance. Ilya Sorokin did the rest of the early work, including his best stop on Charlie Coyle's 25% look in the second, and finished 1.8 goals better than the 29 shots he faced deserved.

Zach Werenski cut it to 2-1 early in the third and briefly gave the Blue Jackets a pulse. Then the Islanders took over the period, out-chancing Columbus 1.68 to 0.54. Schaefer's backhand at 7:01 pushed their win chance from 80% to 94%, Tony DeAngelo finished a 58% chance set up by Mathew Barzal, and Schaefer completed the hat trick on a 61% look at 16:08. Barzal, still being eased back from the knee inflammation he called the "hardest journey of my life" in a New York Post headline, had two assists in under 16 minutes.

The Islanders have won three straight. Columbus has lost five straight in regulation, and the headlines around them are getting heavier: Sean Monahan and Conor Garland are hurt, and Werenski's name now appears in stories asking whether he will reconsider his commitment to the team. That is speculation, not anything he has said, but a fifth straight loss does not make the question go away. Cam Talbot faced 40 shots and allowed exactly what they deserved. He was not the problem.
headline: Schaefer, 19 and counting, buries Columbus
